title: Greece Assumes UN Security Council Presidency for October - World Today News
text:
Greece Assumes UN Security Council Presidency for October
Greece officially assumed the rotating presidency of the United Nations Security Council for the month of October, succeeding France, securitycouncilreport.org reported. Ambassador Aglaia Balta, Greece’s Permanent Representative to the UN, outlined an ambitious provisional programme of work featuring two signature events, two open debates, and crucial scheduled straw polls for the selection of the next UN secretary-general.
Provisional Programme and Two Signature Events Led by Greece
Council members adopted the provisional programme of work on October 1. Guided by the UN Charter and international law, the Greek presidency organized two major signature themes for the month. The first signature event is a high-level briefing scheduled for October 29 on emerging technologies with a primary emphasis on maritime security, under the agenda item concerning the maintenance of international peace and security. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is expected to chair this session.
The second signature event focuses on children and armed conflict, scheduled for October 26. This briefing marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the children and armed conflict mandate by the General Assembly. Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs Giorgos Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting.
Security Council Chairs Open Debates on Women and Middle East
Beyond its signature gatherings, the presidency oversees multiple mandated discussions. The Security Council will hold its annual open debate on women, peace, and security on October 27, titled “Women, peace and security in the next quarter-century: fulfilling the promise through implementation,” which Foreign Minister Gerapetritis is expected to chair. An open debate on the Middle East is scheduled for October 15.
Regional conflicts and peacekeeping transitions demand constant attention from the 15-member body. Addressing the forthcoming drawdown of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon and the threat of a regional power vacuum, Ambassador Balta stated at her press briefing that Greece is assisting the Lebanese Armed Forces to extend their territorial presence.
Security Council Meets with African Union Peace and Security Council
Cooperation between the United Nations and regional bodies takes center stage through a dedicated annual briefing. The 20th annual joint consultative meeting between the Security Council and the African Union Peace and Security Council will take place on October 23. This meeting follows an informal joint seminar held on October 22 in a retreat format at the Greentree Foundation in Manhasset, New York.
African security issues dominate several other legislative files. The Council is scheduled to vote on a draft resolution extending the 1591 Sudan sanctions regime, alongside receiving a regular 120-day briefing featuring insights from UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs officials and Personal Envoy Pekka Haavisto. The Council will address the mandate renewal for the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara ahead of its October 31 expiry, following private meetings with troop-contributing countries and briefings from Special Representative Alexander Ivanko and Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. The bimonthly briefing on Libya and the mandate renewal for the UN Support Mission in Libya are also slated prior to October 31.
Security Council Holds Straw Polls for Next Secretary-General
October may acquire profound institutional significance due to the ongoing process of selecting the next UN secretary-general. Ambassador Balta announced that October is the month to make progress or even agree on a new secretary-general, confirming that slots have been set aside for straw polls in both the first and second halves of the month. The Council will consult all member states regarding the use of color-coded ballots. Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the secretary-general is appointed by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council, meaning any consensus reached this month requires agreement among the five permanent members exercising veto power: China, France, the Russian Federation, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
Managing complex diplomatic negotiations and multilateral administrative mandates often requires specialized advisory support. Organizations and governmental entities engaging with international frameworks frequently rely on specialized public international law firms and diplomatic consultants to manage regulatory compliance and procedural strategies.
International Court of Justice Consultations and Institutional Schedule
On October 2, Council members held an informal interactive dialogue on the implementation of resolution 2744, which strengthened the mandate of the Focal Point for Delisting and re-established the Informal Working Group on General UN Security Council Sanctions Issues. Focal Point for Delisting Yvonne Ching Ling Lee briefed during this session, which was organized jointly by Greece and Pakistan. The Council is also scheduled to hold its annual private meeting with the president of the International Court of Justice, Judge Yuji Iwasawa.
The month-long agenda concludes as the rotating presidency prepares to pass to Latvia in November.
